title: David's fall shows living faith can separate from charity's works for a time
source_text: XL. Ac sane rem ita se habere, & fidem quae nunc viva est & efficax, & per quam aliquis jam justificatus & sanctificatus est, a charitatis aliisque bonis operibus separari posse, & talem evadere, ut habentem non amplius justificet atque sanctificet, convincunt exempla virorum sanctorum, & viva ac salvifica fide proculdubio praeditorum, qui tamen in atrocia scelera inciderunt, & charitati plane repugnantia, & ad tempus notabile in iis perseverarunt; neque tamen propterea simpliciter & absolute infideles facti sunt, & Verbo Dei assensum praebere destiterunt. Ut res clara est in Davide, qui per aliquot menses non solum adulterio se polluit cum uxore Uriae, sed nefandum adulterium, proditione & caede ipsius Uriae viri optimi cumulavit: nec tamen interea fidem omnem Dei Verbo & Legi Mosis denegavit. Quis enim dicere ausit & sustineat, Davidem quamdiu tam diris criminibus indulsit, nihilominus eo ipso tempore dilectionem Dei & proximi retinuisse, & habuisse eam fidem, eumque Dei amorem, quae ipsum Deo placentem redderent, & ad vitam aeternam acceptum, & quae sunt illa conditio cui salus & gloria aeterna promissa est: ac non potius illum, isto temporis intervallo, aeternae damnationis reatu constrictum mansisse?
pass_a_gloss: And truly that the matter stands so — and that faith which is now living and efficacious, and by which someone is already justified and sanctified, can be separated from charity's and other good works, and become such that it no longer justifies and sanctifies the one who has it — is proved by examples of holy men doubtless endowed with living and saving faith, who nevertheless fell into atrocious crimes plainly repugnant to charity, and persevered in them for a notable time; and yet were not thereby made simply and absolutely unbelievers, or ceased to give assent to God's Word. As the matter is clear in David, who for some months not only polluted himself by adultery with Uriah's wife, but heaped the nefarious adultery with betrayal and slaughter of Uriah himself, an excellent man: and yet meanwhile did not deny all faith to God's Word and Moses' Law. For who would dare say and maintain that David, as long as he indulged such dreadful crimes, nevertheless at that very time retained love of God and neighbor, and had that faith and that love of God which would render him pleasing to God and accepted to eternal life — which are that condition to which salvation and eternal glory are promised — and not rather that in that interval of time he remained bound under the guilt of eternal damnation?
pass_b_english: Saints' falls prove living justifying faith can for a time lose charity's works without becoming absolute unbelief.
David's months of adultery and Uriah's murder (2 Samuel 11) kept Word-assent yet not saving love — under damnation-guilt for that interval.

lemmas.gloss: under the guilt of eternal damnation

choices.why: Assent can remain without living love.
